question: Does the desk's Kimi deployment, asked through Chat Completions with no format enforced, answer twenty reads in the form advice-answer/1 asks; what does each body hold, which model does it name, and does its cost at the configured prices agree with Azure's own figure?
pass: Written before the run, in issue 1036 at 2026-11-20T18:50Z, nothing having run (trial TA6 of decision 0224's plan). The requests left the desk, the Mac mini's network and the desk Python's LibreSSL, not a GitHub runner, with the desk resource's own key read in-process from the desk keychain and never printed, logged or written (the Builder's ruling (a)). The code is the build's own, from harness/advise-asks-the-readers-390 with trial P-74's rewording: harness.advise.one, adapters/azure.Live, adapters/advice.read; the reader config/harness.json's kimi (deployment and model kimi-k3.1-pro, chat, output cap 40,000) at xhigh; the prompt harness.advise.prompt_of over an empty rules folder; five diffs, one per commit on canary branch trial/p-75, p75/a_retry.py, b_cache.py, c_paths.py, d_dates.py, e_auth.py, each read four times. Pass: at least 18 of 20 parse whole against advice-answer/1, advice.read giving completed; every body has model, choices[0].finish_reason, usage.prompt_tokens and usage.completion_tokens; the model named is recorded; the twenty's cost at the configured $3 and $15 a million is within a factor of two of Azure's own figure, which the desk session reads and the Builder relays, owed till then. Result, round 1: every one of the twenty answered 200, finish_reason stop, and named the model Kimi-K3.1, not kimi-k3.1-pro, so advice.read gave failed, not_the_model, for all twenty: none completed, and the plan's condition fails as written. harness/1, as the advise step's branch then had it, could not pin that name: a model there was lower case alone. Each body held model, choices[0].finish_reason and usage with prompt_tokens and completion_tokens (both taken out of the fixture by tools.redact_trial, which removes every field named for tokens; their places are in removed) and total_tokens: 72,380 in round 1, 3,619 a read, and 69,057 in round 2. Round 2, twenty more reads of the same five diffs, each prompt built afresh (of the same length, its sha256 another, as a prompt's markers carry a code made anew), with the build's parser asked of each answer's text whatever model it names (advice._chat then advice._answered, unchanged): 20 of 20 are one advice-answer/1, whole, with 1 to 3 findings each. So Kimi answered round 2 in the form with no format enforced. Round 1's texts, refused at the pin first, were not parsed, so whether they would have parsed is not measured. Cost: no read was priced, since the parser prices only the pinned model. At the configured $3 and $15 a million, the forty reads' 141,437 total tokens come to between $0.42, were all of them prompt, and $2.12, were all completion: the split is in the two counts the redaction takes out, so the fixture cannot price the reads closer. Nor does it keep the output cap sent, max_completion_tokens: the 40,000 is the configuration's. Azure's figure is owed. Failed as written. What follows, by the Builder's ruling (b) of 2026-11-20, made after the run: the pin is written as the answers write it, Kimi-K3.1, and compared exactly, harness/1 and advice/1 taking a model's capitals (the build's pin and configuration parts). The answers name Kimi-K3.1, with no Pro, though the deployment is named kimi-k3.1-pro; which model it serves Azure's answer says no more than that. What is kept (2026-11-21, to fit the review's size bound): of the forty reads, the first read of each of the five diffs in each round, ten exchanges; each kept call states all four reads of its diff in that round, the model each named, its finish_reason, its token total, what advice.read and the parser gave, and the sha256 of each dropped exchange as it was recorded whole, so every count the verdict rests on is still read from the fixture. Every prompt and every text of an answer is written as its length in bytes and sha256.
